name: Treaty with the Menominee, 1832 (Green Bay agreement to the Senate's terms)
aka: Agreement at the Agency House, Green Bay, October 27, 1832
promises: First article: the Menominee accepted the Senate's proviso to the 1831 treaty granting three townships on the east side of Lake Winnebago to the Stockbridge, Munsee and Brothertown, with payment for their improvements.

Second article: the Menominee refused the Senate's new line on the west side of the Fox River and instead agreed to cede a differently bounded strip along the southwestern side of the New York Indians' tract, with an equal quantity taken off its northeastern side on the Oconto creek, so the New York Indians' grant stayed at no more than 500,000 acres.

Third article: once the Senate ratified the 1831 treaty with these changes, every article of it would bind both parties as if approved when first agreed, so the Menominee would receive the benefits of the 1831 treaty.
The commissioner delivered presents of clothing worth $1,000, corn, pork and flour at the council.
today: No court, Indian Claims Commission or government finding about this agreement was found. Its preamble records that the Menominee chiefs at first 'in the most positive and decided manner' refused the Senate's terms and agreed to these modifications only after 'much labor and pains, entreaty and persuasion'. By the 1836 Treaty of the Cedars the Menominee released the United States from the provisions of the 1831 and 1832 treaties requiring payment of farmers, blacksmiths and millers, in return for $76,000 to be invested for them.

openQuestions: The Oklahoma State University Indian Claims Commission collection returns no decisions for menominee, menomonee, menomini or menominees, so the Menominee's own claims cases (which may be filed under another title or have gone to the Court of Claims) were not reached. A pass through the Commission's 1978 Final Report docket list is needed before this file is settled.

The Emigrant New York Indians claims (Court of Claims, 177 Ct. Cl. 263, 1966) concern the lands set apart for the New York Indians by the 1831 and 1832 Menominee treaties; they are claims of those Indians, not the Menominee, and were not opened.
Search results show the Menominee Indian Tribe of Wisconsin's website has pages for the 1836 and 1848 treaties (not opened); none was found for 1831 or 1832 (Treaty1832 returned 404 on 2026-11-08).
2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Menominee (Court of Claims index) and 'Menominee 1832 Green Bay' (ICC); nothing on this agreement.
